term.def: A foundation model is a large AI system trained on broad data that can later be adapted for many different business tasks.

prompt.prompt: List three questions to ask before adopting a new foundation model for [business function], covering security, cost, and data privacy.

quiz.q: A foundation model can be fine-tuned later for different uses after its initial training.
quiz.why: This is how foundation models are commonly used across industries once trained.

quiz.q: AI models always need a live internet connection to function.
quiz.why: Many AI models can run on local devices or offline once installed, without constant internet access.

quiz.q: A foundation model is designed to do only one narrow task and nothing else.
quiz.why: Foundation models are built broadly on purpose, so they can be adapted to many different tasks later.
